title: Finite cohomological dimension on affine-diagonal schemes
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact scheme over a field k with affine diagonal [def-weil-field] [def-pc-scheme]. There is an integer d_X >= 0 such that H^p(X,F)=0 for every quasi-coherent O_X-module F [pqf-def-coherent] and every p>d_X.

source.place: Tag 01XI, Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma coherent-lemma-vanishing-nr-affines, finite cohomological dimension for quasi-coherent modules

proof.text: Because X is quasi-compact, choose a finite affine open cover X=U_1 union ... union U_N. Since the diagonal of X over Spec(k) is affine, every finite intersection U_{i_0} cap ... cap U_{i_p} is affine, by the affine-diagonal intersection lemma.

source.place: Tag 01XI, proof of coherent-lemma-vanishing-nr-affines: finite affine covering and affine intersections

proof.text: Order the index set {1,...,N}. By the alternating Cech complex lemma, the Cech cohomology of this cover is the cohomology of the alternating complex, whose degree-p term is the product of F(U_{i_0...i_p}) over strictly increasing tuples i_0<...<i_p in {1,...,N}. There is no such tuple when p >= N, so the alternating complex is zero in degrees p >= N, and Cech cohomology of the cover vanishes in every degree p >= N.

source.place: Tag 01XI, second proof of coherent-lemma-vanishing-nr-affines: alternating Cech complex (Cohomology, Lemma cohomology-lemma-alternating-usual) vanishes in degrees >= t

proof.text: By the Cech comparison theorem for a cover whose finite intersections are affine, Cech cohomology agrees with H^p(X,F) for every quasi-coherent F. Therefore H^p(X,F)=0 for p >= N. Taking d_X=N-1 proves the claimed uniform bound.
